frames.label: Smaller router bits can be run at higher feed rates, while larger bits must be run slower
frames.main_point: Smaller router bits can be run at higher feed rates, while larger bits must be run slower. The overall removal rate is constrained by the router motor’s cutting capacity, not primarily by bit diameter.
frames.source_quote: If you have a smaller cutter you can move the cutter faster; if you have a larger cutter you will have to move it slower.  The limiting factor is how fast the motor can cut wood.

frames.label: Extremely small cutters can require feed rates higher than a CNC router can achieve, and extremely large cutters may...
frames.main_point: Extremely small cutters can require feed rates higher than a CNC router can achieve, and extremely large cutters may need speeds so low the machine struggles to control them accurately. Staying within a mid-range of cutter diameters avoids these machine speed limitations.
frames.source_quote: Obviously if you use an extremely thin cutter your CNC machine won't be able to move fast enough, and if you use an extremely large cutter it will have difficulty accurately controlling the speed low enough, but over a broad range of cutter sizes it shouldn't much matter.
frames.subject: machine speed control limits at extreme cutter diameters
